questions.q: Enzyme used for removing oily stains from the clothes :
questions.solution:
**Lipases** digest fats and oils, so they are added to detergent formulations to remove **oily stains** from laundry.

Pectinase clears fruit juices, protease digests protein stains, and cellulase acts on cellulose.

questions.q: Which of the following micro-organism is used for production of citric acid in industries ?
questions.solution:
**Aspergillus niger**, a fungus, is used for the industrial production of **citric acid**.

Lactobacillus produces lactic acid, and Rhizopus is used for fumaric acid.

questions.q: Milk is converted into curd by:
questions.solution:
**Lactobacillus** (lactic acid bacteria) converts milk sugar into **lactic acid**, which coagulates and partially digests milk proteins to form curd.

It also raises the vitamin B12 content of curd.

questions.q: Roquefort cheese is ripened by growing which fungus on it?
questions.solution:
Roquefort cheese is ripened by **Penicillium roqueforti**, which gives it its flavour and blue veins.

Penicillium notatum is the source of penicillin.

**Alexander Fleming** (1928) noticed that a mould, Penicillium notatum, stopped the growth of Staphylococcus on his culture plate.

Chain and Florey later developed penicillin into a usable drug.

questions.q: Statins, used to lower blood cholesterol, are produced by the yeast:
questions.solution:
**Statins** come from the yeast **Monascus purpureus**. They competitively inhibit the enzyme of cholesterol synthesis.

Trichoderma polysporum gives cyclosporin A, an immunosuppressant used in organ transplants.

questions.q: The main component of biogas is:
questions.solution:
Biogas is produced by **methanogens** (e.g. Methanobacterium) acting anaerobically on cattle dung and organic waste. It is mostly **methane**, with CO2, and traces of H2S and hydrogen.

Methane is the combustible part used as fuel.

questions.q: The bacterium used as a biocontrol agent against caterpillars (Bt) is:
questions.solution:
**Bacillus thuringiensis** produces a crystal (Cry) protein toxin. In the alkaline gut of the larva it becomes active and kills the insect.

Its spores are sprayed on crops, and its gene is used in Bt cotton.

questions.q: Cyclosporin A, used as an immunosuppressive agent in organ transplant patients, is produced by:
questions.solution:
**Cyclosporin A** is produced by the fungus **Trichoderma polysporum**. It suppresses the immune response so that a transplanted organ is not rejected.

Monascus purpureus gives statins.

questions.q: The large holes in Swiss cheese come from CO2 produced by which bacterium? (genus name)
questions.solution:
Swiss cheese is ripened by **Propionibacterium shermanii**, which releases large amounts of CO2 that form the holes ('eyes').

The genus name is enough here.

questions.q: Name the 'clot buster' enzyme obtained from Streptococcus.
questions.solution:
**Streptokinase**, produced by Streptococcus and now modified by genetic engineering, dissolves blood clots in the vessels of patients after a heart attack.

It is therefore called a clot buster.

questions.q: Name the free-living aerobic nitrogen-fixing bacterium used as a biofertilizer.
questions.solution:
**Azotobacter** lives freely in the soil and fixes atmospheric nitrogen aerobically, enriching the soil.

Rhizobium, by contrast, fixes nitrogen symbiotically in root nodules of legumes; Clostridium is free-living but anaerobic.

questions.q: Which genus of yeast is used for the commercial production of ethanol and in bread making?
questions.solution:
**Saccharomyces cerevisiae** (brewer's / baker's yeast) ferments sugars into ethanol and CO2.

In bread the CO2 makes the dough rise; in industry the ethanol is the product.

questions.q: In which stage of sewage treatment (primary, secondary or tertiary) do aerobic microbes digest the organic matter?
questions.solution:
Primary treatment is physical: filtration and sedimentation remove solids. In **secondary (biological) treatment** the effluent is aerated and aerobic microbes form flocs that consume organic matter, lowering the BOD.

The sludge then goes to anaerobic digesters, which yield biogas.

questions.q: Describe the role of microbes in the treatment of sewage, explaining primary and secondary treatment.
questions.solution:
**Sewage** is municipal waste water containing large amounts of organic matter and microbes. It is treated in sewage treatment plants before release.

**Primary treatment (physical).** Floating debris is removed by sequential filtration; grit and soil are removed by sedimentation. The settled solids form the **primary sludge** and the liquid above is the **primary effluent**.

**Secondary treatment (biological).** The primary effluent is passed into large **aeration tanks** and agitated mechanically while air is pumped in. Useful aerobic microbes grow vigorously as **flocs** (bacteria with fungal filaments). They consume the organic matter, so the **BOD** of the effluent falls sharply.

When BOD has fallen enough, the effluent goes to a settling tank where the flocs settle as **activated sludge**. A part is returned to the aeration tank as inoculum; the rest goes to **anaerobic sludge digesters**, where anaerobic bacteria digest it and release **biogas** (methane, H2S, CO2).

The treated effluent is released into rivers and streams. Thus microbes purify water and also yield fuel.
